maya: Quick checklist for tenant enablement: caching/batching/streaming tips to avoid trial flakiness and reduce renewal risk. Posting for field ops.

sam: Nice — do you have concrete checks I can run during kickoff?

maya: Short 5-min health check:
- Verify prefix cache warm: run curl to /v1/prefill (see below)
- Confirm client-side retry/backoff config
- Batch sizing: target 4–16 tokens/request per user
- Streaming: fallback to non-stream path for >10s latencies
- Capture first-10-request quality samples for evals

jordan: Can you paste the curl? I'll run during customer kickoff.

maya: ```
# warm cache for tenant 12345
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/prefill \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"tenant_id":"12345","prompts":["hello","order status sample"]}'
```

eka: Tech notes:
- Set KV TTL >= onboarding window (recommend 12h for trials)
- Eviction policy: prefer LRU with per-tenant caps (1M keys)
- Batching: use max_batch_bytes 512KB + dynamic latency window 20ms
- If using quantized models, allow a short cold-start warmup (30–60s) before live demo

sam: Good call. For renewal risk flags, what signals should we wire to CS dashboard?

maya: Quick list for signals:
- Sustained latency > 1s on first 3 requests
- Quality regression on first-10 samples (eval drop > 5%)
- Prefill failing (5xx) or token limits hit
- Low usage after onboarding (weekly MAU < threshold)

jordan: I'll add alerts in our playbook and tag accounts that match.

onboard-bot: Updated playbook: https://docs.internal/redwood/cs/tenant-touchpoints (v1.2) :link:

maya: Action items:
- Sam: run the 5-min health check during next 10 kickoffs
- Eka: add batch + TTL defaults to onboarding template
- Jordan: wire alerts and a renewal-risk tag

maya: tagging @team-cs for visibility :eyes:
